extracted.intended_audience: users of the SINGULAR computer algebra system (researchers/graduate students/practitioners doing tropical geometry and matroidal realizability computations)
extracted.subtask_description: Documentation of SINGULAR library procedures (realizationMatroids.lib and tropical.lib) for deciding relative realizability of tropical fan curves and for other tropical-geometry computations; describes usage, assumptions, return formats, options, and warnings for each routine.

rubrics_metrics.name: vertexAdjacencyGraph — usage & return format
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: vertexAdjacencyGraph(p); p polytope. Returns a list whose first entry is a bigintmat containing all vertices as row vectors (assigning all vertices an integer). The second entry is a list of intvecs representing the adjacency graph of the vertices of p: the intvec in position i contains all vertices j which are connected to vertex i via an edge of p.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example provided showing call on polytopeViaPoints(M) and the printed first (vertex matrix) and second (adjacency lists) entries. Use this format to index and iterate vertex adjacencies; no other return variants mentioned.

rubrics_metrics.name: vertexEdgeGraph — usage & return format
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: vertexEdgeGraph(p); p polytope. Returns a list where the first entry is a bigintmat containing all vertices as row vectors, and the second entry is a list of intvecs representing the edge graph: each intvec represents an edge of p connecting vertex i with vertex j.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example shows printed vertex matrix and printed list of edges as pairs (i,j). Use this to enumerate edges explicitly rather than adjacency lists.

rubrics_metrics.name: visual — visualization precondition
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: visual(f); f fan or visual(p); p polytope. Assume ambientDimension(f) resp ambientDimension(p) is less or equal 3. Return: none (side-effect: display).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The procedure is for 3D-or-less fans/polytopes only. Examples comment out visual calls. If ambient dimension > 3, visualization is not supported by this routine.

rubrics_metrics.name: realizationMatroids.lib — purpose & domain
rubrics_metrics.description: Purpose: Deciding Relative Realizability for Tropical Fan Curves in 2-Dimensional Matroidal Fans. The library provides procedures deciding relative realizability for one-dimensional weighted balanced polyhedral fans (tropical fan curves) contained in two-dimensional matroidal fans trop(Y) where Y is a projective plane.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notation: inputs represent cones as intvectors w whose equivalence class [w] in R^n/<1> can be written as [w] = m*[v] where [v] is the primitive generator and m the weight. The library restricts to algebraic curves in Y of degree deg(C) whose tropicalization should agree with C.

rubrics_metrics.name: realizationDim — input format, assumptions, and return
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: realizationDim(I,C); I is a homogeneous linear ideal defining the projective plane Y = V(I) and C is a list of intvectors each representing a one-dimensional cone in the tropical fan curve (representation: vector w with [w]=m*[v]). Return: the dimension of the relative realization space of C with respect to Y, and -1 if the relative realization space is empty.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example demonstrates constructing ring, ideal I, and list C of intvecs. Ensure C uses the described representation and I defines a projective plane; output -1 indicates non-realizability.

rubrics_metrics.name: irrRealizationDim — irreducible realizability check
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: irrRealizationDim(I,C); same input format as realizationDim. Returns the dimension of the irreducible relative realization space of C with respect to Y, and -1 if the irreducible realization space is empty.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use when one needs irreducible realizations only. Example shows realizationDim returning 0 while irrRealizationDim returns -1 for the same input, illustrating the distinction.

rubrics_metrics.name: realizationDimPoly — returns example polynomial when realizable
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: realizationDimPoly(I,C); with same input assumptions. If the relative realization space is non-empty, returns the tuple (r,f) where r is the dimension of the relative realization space and f is an example of a homogeneous polynomial of degree deg(C) cutting out a curve X in Y which tropicalizes to C. If empty, returns -1.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples show outputs like '0 x(1)^2+2*x(1)*x(2)+x(2)^2' and larger-dimensional examples returning both dimension and an explicit polynomial. Use this to obtain constructive witness polynomial when realizable.

rubrics_metrics.name: tropical.lib — purpose, main tools, and overall warnings
rubrics_metrics.description: Purpose: computations in tropical geometry. Main tools include tropicalLifting (constructs points in V(I) over Puiseux-series corresponding to tropical points), puiseuxExpansion, drawTropicalCurve, drawTropicalNewtonSubdivision, tropicalJInvariant, jInvariant, weierstrassForm, etc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Warnings: tropicalLifting only works on LINUX and requires gfan; drawTropicalCurve and drawTropicalNewtonSubdivision require LINUX plus latex and xdg-open. For tropicalLifting the parameter t must be a variable in the basering, while for other procedures t may be a parameter. The library often replaces C{{t}} by Q(t) or Q[t], forbidding rational exponents for t; Singular forbids negative exponents of monomials, so integer vectors v_i must have non-negative entries unless one passes directly to tropicalisations. These limitations should be considered when preparing inputs.

rubrics_metrics.name: tropicalLifting — assumptions, options, and detailed return structure
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: tropicalLifting(i,w,ord[,opt]); i ideal in Q[t,x1,...,xn], w intvec, ord int, opt string. Assume (w1/w0,...,wn/w0) is in the tropical variety of i; w0 may NOT be ZERO. The basering should not have parameters and should have a global monomial ordering; the first variable of the basering is treated as the parameter t.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Options (strings): 'isZeroDimensional','isPrime','isInTrop','oldGfan','findAll','noAbs','puiseux','noResubst'. If 'findAll' not set, returns a list l with l[1]=ring Q[a]/m[[t]] or Q[X(...)]/m[[t]], l[2]=int N (meaning t must be replaced by t^(1/N)), l[3]=intvec for exponent-shifts, l[4]=list of strings (generators with coordinates replaced) unless 'noResubst' set. If 'findAll' set, returns a list of such lists (all liftings) when ideal zero-dimensional. Remarks: requires GFAN installed (use 'oldGfan' for GFAN<0.3.0), requires absPrimdecGTZ in primdec.lib unless 'noAbs' used (but 'noAbs' avoids costly absolute primary decomposition), procedure finishes with probability one over Q, and there are important caveats if using Z/pZ base fields (Puiseux series over algebraic closure of Z/pZ not algebraically closed, absolute primdec fails in positive characteristic). Use displayTropicalLifting for nicer output.

rubrics_metrics.name: displayTropicalLifting — display & substitution option
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: displaytropcallifting(troplift[,#]); troplift is the output of tropicalLifting; optional parameter '#' can be the string 'subst'. The procedure displays the output of tropicalLifting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If 'subst' is provided, the lifting is substituted into the ideal and the substituted result is displayed. Example outputs include the ring in which the lifting lives (e.g., Q[[t^(1/2)]]) and printed parametrisations; use this to verify that the lift satisfies the defining ideal.

rubrics_metrics.name: puiseuxExpansion — assumptions and return format
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: puiseuxExpansion(f,n,#); f poly in two variables, n int (number of terms), optional '#' can be 'subst'. Preconditions: f is non-constant, not divisible by the first variable, and squarefree as a power series over C; base field must be Q or a finite extension; monomial ordering is assumed local.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Returns a list where each entry l describes the Newton-Puiseux parametrisations of one branch up to order n: l[i][1]=ring containing ideal LIFT, l[i][2]=int N so parametrisation is x=t^N and y=LIFT[1], l[i][3]=string (polynomial when 'subst' used). If base field had a parameter, display shows how the old parameter can be computed from the new one. Requires absPrimdecGTZ in primdec.lib. If f not squarefree it will be replaced by its squarefree part. Best to display via displayPuiseuxExpansion.

rubrics_metrics.name: displayPuiseuxExpansion — display & subst
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: displayPuiseuxExpansion(puiseux[,#]); puiseux is output of puiseuxExpansion; optional '#' can be 'subst'. The procedure displays the computed Puiseux expansions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If 'subst' is given, the expansion is substituted into the polynomial and the result displayed. If the base field had a parameter and minimal polynomial, the display explains how to compute the old parameter from the new one.

rubrics_metrics.name: tropicalCurve — input assumptions and detailed output structure
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: tropicalCurve(tp[,#]); tp is either a list of linear polynomials ax+by+c (a,b integers, c rational) representing a tropical Laurent polynomial (minimum of linear forms), or a polynomial in Q(t)[x,y] defining a tropical plane curve via valuation. Basering must have a global monomial ordering, two variables, and up to one parameter. Optional input '#[1]' set to 'max' treats tp as maximum instead of minimum.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Returns a list where entries l[1..size(l)-1] correspond to vertices. For each vertex i: l[i][1]=x-coordinate, l[i][2]=y-coordinate, l[i][3]=intmat where first row entries j list connected vertices and second row entries give multiplicities, l[i][4]=list of [primitive integer direction vector, multiplicity] for unbounded edges, l[i][5]=polynomial whose monomials mark the Newton polygon vertices taking the common minimum at that vertex. l[size(l)][1] lists boundary points of Newton subdivision, l[size(l)][2] lists interior edges (pairs of integer vectors), l[size(l)][3]=intvec shift to apply when input linear polynomial had negative a or b. Examples show how to read coordinates, adjacency matrices, edge weights, unbounded edge directions and multiplicities, and Newton subdivision data.

rubrics_metrics.name: drawTropicalCurve & drawTropicalNewtonSubdivision — platform and tool requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: drawTropicalCurve and drawTropicalNewtonSubdivision visualize tropical plane curves and Newton subdivisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These visualization routines will only display the tropical curve on LINUX and require latex and xdg-open to be installed. Use drawTropicalCurve only when these external tools are available; otherwise visualization will not function.
